let me go! phrase

also let go of me

classical

Traupman 99, 102
Plaut.

Mitte mē!

Examples

  • In scālīs mōbilibus cum Theodōrus, «Mitte mē, tata!» clāmitāns, manū patris dīmissā sōlus stāre vellet

    When Theo, on the escalator, kept shouting “Let me go, Dad!” and wanted to let go of his hand and stand by himselfLibellus I, Iter in Lūsitāniam

Other words

  • Mitte mē, sīs! — let go of me, please!

    also used · classical · Traupman 99, 102; Plaut.

See also leave me alone!, let go.

SourcesLewis & Short: mitto

John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency: pp. 99, 102, checked against the searchable text of the book on 29 October 2026.
